guides.title: Setting up a bow Projectile Spawn Point
guides.answer:
For a bow, configure the spawn point in the player's **Weapon firing** setup—not in a generic project asset tree.

1. Set **Fire mode** to **Projectile / travelling** and select your saved arrow **Projectile**.
2. Use **EDIT SPAWN POINTS...** to place a launch point at the bow's arrow rest/nocking position, then select it under **Spawn point**. The existing Bow Playground example calls its point `Bow_Nock`.
3. Set **Firing** to **Selected spawn point** and **Fire at** to **Animation start** or **After a delay**. You can also use **SET FIRE TIME IN ANIMATION...**.
4. Choose **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER**, save the level, and test firing.

I can explain any of those controls. I haven't inspected your project or confirmed which bow is selected.

guides.title: Using two projectile spawn points
guides.answer:
Renegade's **Weapon firing** panel supports either one or two authored spawn points.

1. Choose the primary **Spawn point**.
2. Under **Firing**, select **Selected spawn point**, **Alternate between two**, or **Both together**.
3. With Alternate or Both, select **Second spawn point**. That control is normally hidden for single-point firing.
4. Select **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER** to persist the equipment change.

This is an existing capability verified in source and native UX documentation, but I can't see your current equipment settings.

guides.title: Setting projectile release timing
guides.answer:
The **Weapon firing** panel has two ways to control *when* the projectile launches:

1. Under **Fire at**, choose **Animation start** to launch immediately, or **After a delay** to enter **Delay (seconds)**.
2. For a visual match to the animation, select **SET FIRE TIME IN ANIMATION...**. Scrub the preview, use **MARK CURRENT POSE**, then **USE FIRE TIME**.
3. Finish with **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER**, and save the level when satisfied.

The animation marker must occur before the clip ends. The documented Bow Playground proof used a `Bow_Nock` release delay, but your animation may differ.

guides.title: Creating or editing a projectile
guides.answer:
Renegade separates the **projectile asset** from the weapon's **firing setup**.

1. In **Weapon firing**, select **NEW** for a projectile asset or **EDIT COPY** to modify a saved one without overwriting it.
2. In Basic mode choose a starting preset (such as **Arrow** or **Bolt**) and set the model, speed, gravity, impact behaviour and effects.
3. Use **SHOW ADVANCED** for lifetime, rotation, damage and detailed particle settings. Save the projectile, then select it in **Weapon firing** and **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER**.

Not every advanced projectile behaviour is implemented; the documentation specifically warns against assuming homing or rocket explosions.

guides.title: Hitscan versus travelling projectiles
guides.answer:
Renegade supports **two firing modes** in the Weapon firing panel:

- **Projectile / travelling:** launches a saved physical projectile that travels through the scene.
- **Hitscan / instant ray:** checks the aim line instantly, using **Range (metres)** and **Damage** controls, without requiring a projectile asset.

Choose **Fire mode** to switch between them, then **APPLY TO THIS PLAYER** to save the equipment configuration. This describes the implemented editor controls; I haven't checked the selected weapon in your project.

guides.title: Mapping first-person arms and shotgun reload animations
guides.answer:
Renegade pairs **arms** and **weapon** animations inside **First Person Assembly**. The reload setup is separate from projectile firing.

1. Select **Arms product** and **Weapon product**, then **LOAD PARTS**.
2. In **Action slots**, assign the imported Reload clip under the corresponding **arms** and **weapon** action selectors. Use **Preview action** to check the pairing.
3. Open **WEAPON SETTINGS** to adjust **Loaded capacity**, **Minimum shot interval**, and **Allow partial reload**. Use **SAVE CHANGES** or **SAVE AS NEW** when satisfied.

This assumes the clips are already compatible with their rigs. It doesn't retarget animations between different skeletons, and I haven't inspected your asset.
